cards.text: Friend, this one's a letter. It's from Paul to Titus, a man Paul calls his true child in the faith they share. Paul opens by introducing himself as a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ.

cards.question: Paul says he's an apostle for the sake of God's elect. What is his work there for?

answers.text: Their faith and their knowledge of the truth
Their wealth and their standing in town
Their customs and their traditions of old

cards.text: That truth leads to godliness, and Paul mentions the hope of eternal life, which God promised. Friend, a promise is only as good as the one making it.

cards.question: Paul says God promised eternal life. What does Paul say about God that makes that promise sure?
True or false: God made that promise of eternal life before time began.

cards.text: God made that promise before time began, and friend, I can't keep a promise to myself past the snooze button. Then in His own time, God made His word plain through preaching, and that preaching was trusted to Paul.

cards.question: The preaching of God's word was trusted to Paul. By whose command?

cards.text: Paul wishes Titus grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior. Then, with zero small talk, it's straight to business.
Paul reminds Titus why he left him in Crete: to set in order what was unfinished. Paul is the coworker who heads out and leaves the sticky note on your desk that says, "Finish this. Thanks!"

cards.question: Paul also left Titus in Crete to appoint ___ in every town.

cards.text: So what kind of man can be an elder? Paul starts with a big one: he must be blameless.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says an elder's home life doesn't matter, as long as he's blameless at church.
Paul says an elder must be the husband of but one wife. What does he say about the elder's children?

answers.text: They should be grown and married
They should be trained to teach

cards.text: And those children can't be open to accusation of indiscretion or insubordination. Then Paul calls the overseer God's steward, who must be above reproach, and starts a list of what he must NOT be.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says an overseer can be quick-tempered, as long as he's above reproach in everything else.

cards.text: The rest of the NOT list: not self-willed, not given to drunkenness, not violent, not greedy for money. And that quick temper line hits home, because I once yelled at an oven timer for going off ON TIME.

cards.question: Paul flips from what an overseer must NOT be to what he MUST be. True or false: being hospitable makes that list.

cards.text: Also on the list: a lover of good, self-controlled, upright, holy and disciplined. And last, he must hold firmly to the faithful word, just as it was taught.

cards.question: An overseer must hold firmly to the faithful word. What is that for?

answers.text: To encourage others and refute those who contradict it
To win every debate and gain followers in town
To keep the teaching hidden away from outsiders

cards.text: Now Paul tells Titus why he needs men like that. Many are rebellious, full of empty talk and deception, especially those of the circumcision.

cards.question: Paul says these people full of empty talk and deception must be ___.

cards.text: And they're doing real damage. Not one person here and there, baker: ENTIRE households get undermined, and they teach things they should not.

cards.question: These teachers are undermining entire households. What does Paul say they're doing it for?

cards.text: Then Paul quotes one of their own prophets: “Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy gluttons.”

cards.question: Paul has just quoted what that prophet said. True or false: Paul says the saying is true.
Paul calls that prophet's testimony true. So what does he tell Titus to do?
Paul tells Titus to rebuke them sternly. What's the goal?

answers.text: So they will be sound in the faith
So the whole town sees them shamed
So they will leave the church for good

cards.text: That stern rebuke has a second goal too: there are some things they need to tune out. Think of hitting mute on a group chat that will NOT stop buzzing.

cards.question: Paul wants them to pay no attention to Jewish ___ or to commands from men who have rejected the ___.

cards.text: Then Paul drops a line short enough for me to stamp on a cookie: to the pure, all things are pure.

cards.question: To the pure, all things are pure. But to the defiled and unbelieving, ___ is pure.
True or false: Paul says the minds of the defiled are still clean, even though their consciences aren't.

cards.text: Last, Paul sums these men up. They profess to know God.

cards.question: These men profess to know God. What does Paul say gives them away?

cards.text: Saying one thing and doing another is like texting "On my way!" while you're still under the covers. Except Paul's words for it are a lot stronger: he calls them detestable and disobedient.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says these men are still fit for some good deeds.
